_comment: Per-platform performance baselines, compared by `cargo run -p sunrise-bench --bin baseline -- --check target/criterion bench/baseline.json 60`. The keys are the rows of BENCHES in crates/sunrise-bench/src/bin/baseline.rs, and a unit test there holds this file to them on every platform. Nothing enforces the values and nothing updates them automatically. The bench-regression job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on schedule and workflow_dispatch only — never on a pull request — on ubuntu-latest and macos-15, carries continue-on-error: true, and passes a 60% tolerance rather than the 5% docs/10-cross-cutting/performance-budgets.md specifies, because on the shared runner the same binary swings +270% (ws_handshake, since renamed sync_session) and −39% (submit_create_task) against its own recorded baseline. So this file is edited by hand, from the values `baseline` prints, in a commit that says what changed and why, and _provenance says where each platform's values were taken. A null is a metric never measured on that platform. See performance-budgets.md §Regression policy and https://github.com/justin13888/Sunrise/issues/33.

_provenance.darwin-aarch64: Apple M3 Pro (12 cores, 36 GB), macOS 26.6.1, rustc 1.91.1, at the commit that added these values (#473): `SUNRISE_BENCH_COMPACT_TASKS=10000 cargo bench -p sunrise-bench --benches -- --warm-up-time 2 --measurement-time 5`, then `cargo run -p sunrise-bench --bin baseline`. A laptop, not the macos-15 runner the nightly leg compares on; #474 re-records from that runner.
_provenance.linux-x86_64: The four pre-existing values are carried from earlier hand edits. The keys added in #473 are null until the nightly ubuntu-latest leg reports them (#474).
